**Test image**: Soybean seed on white background. One healthy tan seed (top-left), one seed with dark brown/black rough/crumbly texture covering the upper 2/3, while the lower portion remains normal tan.

**Key observations**:
- This is a **seed symptom** (harvested seed, not leaf/stem/root)
- Dark brown-black discoloration with rough, crumbly texture — suggests fungal mycelium/pycnidia on seed surface
- Partial coverage (top portion affected, base normal)

**Reference comparison**:
- **Phomopsis**: Reference shows pods with pycnidia/dark circular lesions — same fungal genus (Diaporthe/Phomopsis) causes seed decay with dark rough surface appearance
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Shows purple/violet discoloration but smoother texture — test seed is darker/rougher
- **Anthracnose**: Pod/stem symptoms, dark lesions possible on seeds
- **Diaporthe**: Reference showed stem canker symptoms (not seed)
- All others (Cercospora, Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, White_Mold, etc.) primarily target leaves/stems/roots

The dark rough texture with pycnidia-like surface on the seed most closely matches **Phomopsis seed decay** (Diaporthe phaseolorum), which is the most common soybean seed disease causing dark discoloration with fungal structures on the seed coat.
